name: brainfuck
why: An interpreter for the famous minimal esoteric language, a fun small detour into how little a language needs.

brief.what_it_is: A Brainfuck interpreter written in C. It runs Brainfuck source files passed on the command line, or code passed directly with -e, and with no arguments it opens an interactive console. It also ships a C API (brainfuck.h) for parsing Brainfuck strings and executing them against a tape context from your own program. The README does not spell out the output format, so the notes cannot say more about what it prints beyond the example programs.
brief.why_it_exists: The README gives no stated motivation. It describes the project only as a Brainfuck interpreter written in C, with a collection of example programs in the examples/ directory.
brief.how_it_works: The README does not explain the internals. It shows a C program that creates a state with brainfuck_state(), an execution context with brainfuck_context(BRAINFUCK_TAPE_SIZE), parses a string with brainfuck_parse_string, adds it with brainfuck_add, and runs it with brainfuck_execute(state->root, context). The interactive console depends on libedit, which the README names as a dependency.

commands_seen.context: Usage synopsis from the README. -e/--eval runs code directly, -v/--version shows version information, -h/--help shows a help message.
Create the build directory before building out of tree.
Generate the Makefiles from the source root (one level up).
Build the interpreter with the generated build system.
Install the built binaries to the local system; the install prefix is set by CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX.
Run the interpreter directly from the build directory on an example program, without installing.
Download the source (shown in the README with a leading shell prompt, which is dropped here).

brief.install_notes: Building needs CMake and a C compiler such as Clang or GCC. It depends on libedit: install libedit-dev on Debian/Ubuntu, or use the libedit that comes with the macOS Xcode command line tools. The steps are a git clone or zip download, then mkdir build, cd build, cmake .., make, and optionally make install. No accounts or runtimes are mentioned.
brief.standout: The README pairs a tiny Brainfuck interpreter with a documented C API, so you can embed the interpreter in your own C code. It also ships a large examples/ directory of Brainfuck programs, with the README noting an effort to credit original authors.
brief.status: unknown. The README has a GitHub Actions build badge and a long contributor list, but it shows no release dates, last-commit dates, or maintenance notes, and I did not fetch the repository's commit or release pages.
brief.caveats: Written in C and built with CMake, so it needs a C toolchain and libedit before it will compile. The README gives only one C API example and no API reference. The interactive console depends on libedit. The README does not state a license beyond a pointer to LICENSE.txt in the repository, which I did not open; the README says Apache License 2.0.
quotes: The interactive console can be accessed by passing no arguments.
The examples/ directory contains a large amount of brainfuck example programs. We have tried to attribute the original authors of these programs where possible.
